metaDescription: Six reading floor lamps compared on aimable light, dimming and control, from a gooseneck to dual-head torchieres, to suit a favorite chair or bedside.
introParagraphs: A reading lamp has to put the right amount of light on the page without glare in your eyes. The six lamps here take different paths to that goal. The Globe Electric 67134 combines a 72 inch torchiere with a separate adjustable reading light, the marctronic and Yikuneng both offer 18W LED output with remote control, and the O'Bright and WEDEESUN rely on a flexible gooseneck.

The spread in aiming is the key difference. The O'Bright has a flexible gooseneck, a 360 degree rotatable shade and a 10 inch base, the WEDEESUN is a 15W gooseneck with touch control and a 3500K to 7000K range, and the SIBRILLE uses a linen shade with a remote and foot pedal. Brightness ranges from the 1800 lumen marctronic to more modest lamps with a 9W bulb.

We evaluated each lamp on how well it aims light at a page, how smoothly it dims, how easy the controls are and how stable the base is, based on product specs and buyer feedback. Reading is a close-up task, so we favored lamps that place light where the book is and avoid flicker, then ranked them for active adults who read daily.

products.name: Globe Electric 67134 Torchiere with Reading Light

specList.label: Switches
specList.value: Separate on and off for each

products.description:
The Globe Electric 67134 packs two lights in one: a 72 inch torchiere that fills the room with soft light, and an adjustable reading light you aim at the page. Each has its own on and off switch, so you can use the reading light alone or add the torchiere for ambience. A three-way dimmer lets you set the torchiere to low, medium or high.

That pairing is exactly what a reading chair needs, because the room light reduces contrast while the reading light delivers the task brightness. The tradeoff is that the listing describes bulb requirements rather than an included LED setup, so you should confirm what is in the box and choose LED bulbs. The two-switch layout is simple but less modern than a remote-controlled lamp.

Setup is easy, and the silver frosted shade suits many rooms. Compared with the O'Bright, which offers only one gooseneck light, the Globe gives you both room and task lighting. It sits at the lower-middle of the cost range, making it a strong value for a reading corner.
products.bestFor: A reading chair that benefits from both room light and a task light
pros: Torchiere and reading light have separate switches
Three-way dimmer sets low, medium or high room light
Tall 72 inch frame fills a corner
Lower-middle cost for two lights in one
cons: Bulb arrangement needs checking before purchase
No remote control or stepless dimming
Reading light is less powerful than the LED-only lamps

products.name: marctronic 18W 1800LM Floor Lamp with Remote

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: Dimmable, timing, works with smart plug

products.description:
The marctronic is an 18W LED lamp rated at 1800 lumens with a 50 foot remote and touch control. It is dimmable with timing, and the listing says it works with a smart plug. The anti-glare LED design aims to avoid harsh light at eye level.

Its brightness is generous for reading, well above the 400 to 800 lumen target, so you will mostly use it dimmed down. The tradeoff is the lamp is more of a general room reader than a precisely aimed task light, because the light comes from a panel rather than a gooseneck. Touch control carries the usual dry-finger caveat, so the remote is the better route.

A smart plug adds voice or schedule control if you want it. Compared with the Yikuneng, it offers the same 18W class but a longer remote range. It sits in the middle of the cost range.
products.bestFor: Reading with strong, dimmable light and a long-range remote
pros: 1800 lumens gives plenty of reading headroom
Works with a smart plug for scheduling
cons: Panel light is less focused than a gooseneck
Touch control may be unreliable with dry skin
Brightness needs dimming for a small room

products.name: Yikuneng Dimmable LED Reading Floor Lamp
products.description:
The Yikuneng offers stepless dimming from 5 to 100 percent and a color range from 2700K to 6500K, with memory of your last setting. Its RF remote does not need to be pointed at the lamp, and touch control is built in. The listing compares its brightness to a 200W halogen.

For reading, the wide color range is the benefit, because you can choose warm light for a novel and cooler light for small print. The tradeoff is that it lights from a panel rather than a flexible neck, so it is less precise than the O'Bright or WEDEESUN. The many settings take a little while to learn.

At the same cost tier as the marctronic, it trades some remote range for finer tuning. It is a good all-round lamp for a living room reading chair. Compared with the SIBRILLE, it is brighter and more adjustable.
products.bestFor: Readers who like to fine-tune brightness and warmth
cons: Panel light is less focused than a gooseneck
Touch control may be unreliable with dry skin

products.name: WEDEESUN 15W Gooseneck LED Floor Lamp
products.description:
The WEDEESUN is the lowest-cost lamp here and a 15W LED with a 360 degree gooseneck. Brightness runs from 10 to 100 percent, and color temperature from 3500K to 7000K. It is designed with an anti-glare, non-flicker driver and adjustable height and angle.

The gooseneck lets you put the light right on the page, which is what reading needs. The tradeoff is the color range starts at 3500K, so it never gets as warm as the 2700K lamps, and it relies on touch control, which can be unreliable with dry fingertips. It also has no remote, so you adjust it by hand.

For a bedside table or a favorite armchair, it is a practical choice. Compared with the O'Bright, it is cheaper and includes the LED, but it has less premium metal construction. It is a strong pick if you want to aim light at a page.
products.bestFor: Aiming bright, flicker-free light at a page on a budget
pros: 360 degree gooseneck aims light at the page
cons: Color starts at 3500K, so it is never very warm
Touch control only, with no remote
Less premium construction than the O'Bright

products.name: O'Bright Adjustable Gooseneck Floor Lamp
products.description:
The O'Bright is an all-metal adjustable floor lamp with a flexible gooseneck, a 360 degree rotatable shade and a 10 inch base. It uses an E26 socket, so you choose the bulb, and the matte black finish gives it a modern look. The company is based in California and offers direct customer service by phone or email.

The gooseneck is what makes it a reading lamp: you bend it over your shoulder and point the shade at the page. The 10 inch base is wide enough to resist tipping, a size that matches the rule of thumb for stable lamps. The tradeoff is it is the highest-cost pick, and you must supply the bulb and live without a remote.

Because you choose the bulb, you can pick a high-CRI LED with the color and brightness you prefer. Compared with the WEDEESUN, it is sturdier and more flexible in bulb choice but costs more. It is a good long-term lamp.
products.bestFor: Readers who want a durable, repairable lamp with a bulb of their choice
pros: Gooseneck and 360 degree shade aim light well
cons: Bulb choice is up to you

products.name: SIBRILLE Dimmable Floor Lamp with Linen Shade
products.description:
The SIBRILLE is a modern floor lamp with a matte metal base and a linen fabric shade. A 9W bulb is included, so there is no pairing or extra purchase, and it offers three color temperatures. The remote and foot pedal give two ways to control it.

Its linen shade diffuses light softly, which is good for ambience but not as focused as a gooseneck. The 9W bulb is modest, so it suits casual reading rather than long sessions with small print. The tradeoff is less brightness than the 18W lamps.

Compared with the Yikuneng, it is simpler, with fewer settings, and it looks more like furniture. It is a sensible choice for a living room where style matters.
products.bestFor: Casual reading in a living room where the lamp has to look good
cons: 9W bulb is modest for long reading sessions
Linen shade diffuses rather than focuses light

buyingCriteria.explanation: Reading guidance cites 400 to 800 lumens on the reading surface, and the marctronic at 1800 lumens clears that with room to dim. The SIBRILLE's 9W bulb is lower, which is fine for casual reading but not for fine print. Lumens at the lamp are not the same as lumens at the page, so aim and distance matter. Choose a lamp you can place close to the book.

A gooseneck or swivel head lets you point light at the page without moving the lamp. The O'Bright has a flexible gooseneck and a 360 degree shade, and the WEDEESUN offers a 360 degree gooseneck. Panel lamps like the marctronic and Yikuneng spread light more widely. For close work, aimable lamps do better.

Advice varies, with warm 2700K to 3000K for relaxing, 3500K to 4000K for general tasks and 4000K to 5000K for focused reading. The Yikuneng spans 2700K to 6500K, while the WEDEESUN spans 3500K to 7000K. A CRI of 80 or more is the minimum, and 90 or more helps text and color accuracy. Pick a lamp that can reach neutral white.

Cheap LED drivers can flicker, causing headaches during long reading sessions. The WEDEESUN advertises a non-flicker, anti-glare design, and the marctronic uses anti-glare LED technology. A shade or diffuser keeps the bare LED out of view. If you notice flicker at low dimming, try a different bulb.

Physical buttons on the pole beat touch sensors, which can fail with dry skin or poor circulation. The SIBRILLE has a foot pedal, the Globe Electric has separate switches, and the marctronic and Yikuneng have remotes. Choose a control you can operate in the dark without hunting. A remote with a 50 foot range is convenient but easy to lose.

A tall lamp with a long reach needs a stable base, and a base at least 8 inches across is a sensible minimum. The O'Bright has a 10 inch base, which suits its gooseneck, while the Globe Electric is 72 inches tall and needs a stable footprint. Check that the base fits beside your chair. Keep the cord out of walking paths.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light at the page
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated output and light type, from the marctronic's 1800 lumens to the SIBRILLE's 9W bulb. We also looked at whether the lamp can be aimed. A lamp that puts enough light on the page ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Aiming and adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated necks, shades and heads, including the O'Bright's gooseneck and 360 degree shade and the WEDEESUN's gooseneck. Adjustability decides whether you can reach a comfortable reading position. Fixed panels scored lower for close tasks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dimming and color
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dimming range and color temperature, such as the Yikuneng's 5 to 100 percent and 2700K to 6500K range against the Globe Electric's three-way dimmer. Smooth dimming and flexible color suit different books and times of day. Lamps with limited control were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and comfort
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed switches, remotes and pedals for ease of use, including the SIBRILLE's foot pedal and the marctronic's 50 foot remote. Controls that avoid bending and reaching ranked higher. The strongest overall pick, the Globe Electric, offers a simple two-switch layout, while the most basic pick, the WEDEESUN, uses touch only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base size and build against each lamp's relative cost tier. The O'Bright has a 10 inch base and all-metal build but the highest cost, while the WEDEESUN is the lowest cost. We also considered whether a bulb is included.

howToChoose.intro: The light source shape affects how well you can aim it.

cards.label: Gooseneck lamps
cards.text: Goosenecks let you point light at the page. The O'Bright and WEDEESUN are the examples here. Choose them for close reading.

cards.label: Panel and torchiere lamps
cards.text: Panels spread light across a wider area, which is easier on the eyes in a room. The marctronic, Yikuneng, SIBRILLE and Globe Electric fit here. Choose them for chair-side ambience.

cards.label: Our recommendation
cards.text: Pick the WEDEESUN or O'Bright for close print, and the Globe Electric if you also want room light.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A gooseneck or swivel head, a flicker-free driver and a neutral color temperature around 4000K. Position the lamp beside or behind your shoulder to avoid shadows.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WEDEESUN's gooseneck and 3500K to 7000K range suit small print, and the O'Bright lets you choose a high-CRI bulb. The Yikuneng also reaches neutral white.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a durable lamp with your choice of bulb, as the O'Bright offers, or a remote with strong output like the marctronic. A better build lasts for years.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You read casually. The WEDEESUN gives an aimable light at the lowest cost, and the Globe Electric adds room light at a modest tier.

faq.q: Which lamp is best for reading overall?
faq.a: The Globe Electric 67134 is the best overall because it pairs a torchiere with an adjustable reading light on separate switches. If you want remote control and more brightness, the marctronic is a strong alternative. Choose a gooseneck like the WEDEESUN for small print.

faq.q: How many lumens do I need for reading?
faq.a: Guides suggest 400 to 800 lumens on the reading surface, and 1000 or more if the lamp doubles as room light. The marctronic at 1800 lumens has plenty of headroom. A dimmer lets you lower it for comfort.

faq.q: What color temperature is best for reading?
faq.a: Warm 2700K to 3000K is relaxing, but 3500K to 4000K is a good neutral for text, and 4000K to 5000K is better for focused work. The Yikuneng covers the full range. A CRI of 90 or more helps accuracy.

faq.q: Is a gooseneck better than a panel lamp?
faq.a: For close reading, yes, because you can aim the light. Panel lamps spread light more evenly and suit general use. The O'Bright and WEDEESUN are goosenecks, and the others are panels or torchieres.
It helps if the lamp sits behind a chair or sofa. The marctronic offers 50 feet of range, and the Yikuneng has an RF remote. A foot switch or manual control is a good backup.

Cheap LED drivers or incompatible dimmers can cause flicker. Choose a lamp that advertises a non-flicker design, such as the WEDEESUN, or use a quality bulb in the O'Bright. Flicker can cause eye strain.
A base at least 8 inches across helps, and the O'Bright has a 10 inch base. Keep tall lamps like the 72 inch Globe Electric out of high-traffic areas. Route cords along walls.
